title: runCommand executes the never-returning `watch` verb synchronously on the Qt main thread — one console command permanently freezes the kiosk
description: Bridge.runCommand (habit_gui.py:158-164) routes user-typed console text straight into core.cli() with no verb allowlist, on the Qt main/GUI thread. Two subcommands never return: `watch` calls the daemon loop watch() (habit_core.py:1037-1039 -> 646), an unbounded `while True: ... time.sleep(interval)` (habit_core.py:657-673) — verified by execution: cli(['watch','--interval','1']) is still running after 2.5s and never exits — and the `gui` verb spawns a whole second GUI process (habit_core.py:1041-1049). The console's own placeholder and help text invite the operator to run 'the same verbs your agent uses', and `watch` is a documented agent verb (docs/design/habit_tracker_architecture.md lists `watch --headless` in the subagent surface), so an operator typing `watch` (or `watch --headless`) in the Console tab freezes the entire kiosk UI forever: the slot blocks inside time.sleep, Qt never returns to the event loop, the screensaver/idle logic stops, and touch input is dead until systemd restarts the service (Restart=on-failure does not fire — the process is alive, merely hung). On a battery/solar kiosk this is a total, field-unrecoverable UI outage indistinguishable from device failure. Note `watch` is also the service's own daemon verb (awso-habit.service ExecStart=/opt/awso/habitctl watch), making it the most natural thing for an operator to try from the console. Fix shape: allowlist console verbs to the interactive set (add/check/due/list/mode/sos/chat/events/report/status/...) or at minimum reject `watch`/`gui`, and/or run cli() on a worker thread with a timeout. This is a hang, not resource exhaustion: the defect is a blocking call with no return path on the UI thread, triggered by a single documented verb from the designed console surface.
repro_hints: Repro harness: C:/Users/ala/AppData/Local/Temp/mantis_repro/repro.py section 'F-04 watch verb never returns' — cli(['--db', tmp, 'watch', '--interval', '1']) launched in a thread is still alive after 2.5s (never returns). For the full effect on the device: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 habit_gui.py --selfcheck --db <tmp> and call bridge.runCommand('watch') — the check QTimer never fires because the main thread is blocked in time.sleep.
reasoning: Verified against habit_gui.py:158 (Bridge.runCommand): console text is split and passed straight to core.cli() with no verb allowlist, on the Qt main thread. `watch` (habit_core.py, watch()) is a `while True` loop with time.sleep — typed into the Console tab it blocks the event loop forever; on a battery kiosk this is an unrecoverable UI hang. Not fixed in the current tree; out of scope of the layout task but confirmed still present. Recommend the fix shape from the finding: interactive verb allowlist (reject watch/gui) and/or worker-thread execution.

The never-returning watch() loop can no longer be reached from the GUI console.
